Today, tax automation has a shared `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations` core with vendor adapters underneath it. **Instead is the only registered adapter.** GruntWorx already has a provider enum value, but that does not make it operational; Juno still uses a legacy path outside the registry.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

The shared layer owns the operations and rules that apply across vendors:

| Area | Shared responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Authorization and connections | Start and complete authorization; read, disconnect, renew, revoke and verify grants; disconnect all grants during firm lifecycle events |
| Export | Authorize access, validate documents against capabilities, create/reuse the tax-preparation envelope and send records, then invoke the adapter |
| Recovery | Resume failed sends after reconnect or successful grant verification; periodically reconcile stale processing statuses |
| Status reporting | Accept normalized processing statuses, enforce state transitions and broadcast changes after commit |
| Data lifecycle | Delete preparations for clients/contacts, merge contact preparations and clean up firm data |
| Infrastructure | OAuth token handling, HTTP transport/error handling, presigned upload transfer, async operations and metrics |

The export boundary is explicit: core creates the shared records, then calls the selected adapter’s `ExportAsync`. Instead schedules its own workflow after the surrounding transaction commits. See [shared export](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53) and [Instead export](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/export_async.rb:28).

**Registration and the adapter contract**

[Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:10) contains:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = {instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead}.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = {instead: :tax_automations_instead}.freeze
```

It selects an adapter from the firm’s `FirmSettings.provider`, or from an explicitly supplied provider during authorization and background work. Unknown providers raise `UnknownProviderError`. A provider without a feature-flag entry is considered available by that flag check.

The interface is expressed through Ruby constants and production dispatch sites. Under an adapter namespace `A`, callers expect:

| Required member | Invocation |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | `.for_firm(firm)`, `.usable_for(firm)`, `.capabilities`, plus ActiveRecord queries such as `.connected`, `.installed`, `.where`, `.find` |
| `Client` | `.new(connection)`; shared grant services call `renew!` and `revoke_tokens!` |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` → authorization URL result |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` → connection result |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)` |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(user, actor, connection, {tax_automation_document_ids: ...})` |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)` |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id)` |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` |

The last four are important parts of the contract beyond connect/send: they are called by [reconciliation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:34), [preparation deletion](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/batch_destroy.rb:48), [firm cleanup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firms/destroy_cleanup.rb:53) and [contact merging](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/merge_for_contact.rb:89).

Instead’s `Connection` includes `HasOauthConnection` and `HasCapabilities`; its `Client` inherits `BaseClient`, which includes `TokenRefreshable`. The adapter declares OAuth settings and implements vendor vocabulary and mappings. If it uses the shared presigned-upload service, its client also needs `upload_to_signed_target`.

Connection classes must live directly under their registered namespace: `Registry.client_for` derives the adapter from `connection.class.module_parent`.

Provider switching is handled centrally. Starting authorization preserves the existing connection; successful completion updates settings, binds the external tenant/account and disconnects the displaced grant within the transaction. See [Connections::Create](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:43).

**The capability passport**

The passport is a class-level, validated `Dry::Struct` returned by `Connection.capabilities`. It describes the vendor independently of a particular grant:

```text
Capabilities
  terms[]
    return_type
    accepted_file_formats[]
    max_file_size_mb
  supported_tax_years[]
```

Adapters supply private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`. Formats and size limits belong to each return type, allowing different rules for different forms. Supported return types are derived from the terms.

Validation rejects duplicate return-type declarations, malformed formats, nonpositive integer size limits, and years outside `2000..Date.current.year + 1`. Missing implementations fail when `.capabilities` is called. See [HasCapabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:18).

Instead currently declares the 11 mapped forms—1040, 1120, 1120S, 1065, 1041, 706, 709, 990, 5500, 2290 and 1120F—with shared format/size settings and the current year plus the preceding two years.

Core uses the passport to reject unsupported forms, years, file extensions and sizes before adapter dispatch. The API presents it as `tax_years` and `return_types`, enriching each form with its label, personal/business classification, `file_types` and `file_size_limit`. See [validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:41) and [serialization](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:59).

**Data model**

| Entity | Role and identity |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One row per firm: selected provider and external tenant binding. Provider values are `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2`. |
| Adapter `Connection` | Vendor grant and encrypted credentials. Instead has one per firm, a polymorphic staff creator, and PKCE verifier storage. |
| Shared `TaxPreparation` | Return envelope containing client/contact, year, current return type, EIN and business name. It still uses the physical `juno_tax_preparations` table. |
| Shared `TaxAutomations::Document` | Send record linking a source document to an envelope and provider. Uniqueness is `(firm, tax_preparation, document, provider, return_type)`. |
| Instead `Entity` | Persistent vendor taxpayer handle: external UUID, entity type, local client/contact linkage, source and sync/archive metadata. |
| Instead `Document` | Vendor extension of one shared send record: entity linkage, upload path and external file UUID. |

The envelope lookup key is **firm + client + contact + year**, excluding provider and return type. A subsequent export can update its current return type. Each send record therefore snapshots both **provider and return type**, preserving its original destination.

Send records have two separate state machines:

- Upload: `waiting → uploading → uploaded`, with failure/reset paths and `uploaded_at`.
- Processing: `sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`.

A shared failure reason accompanies these states. Vendor status translation belongs in the adapter; core stores and broadcasts the normalized result.

Sources: [settings](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firm_settings.rb:6), [envelope lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/find_or_create.rb:95), [send model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:8), [Instead entity](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/entity.rb:5), [Instead document](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/document.rb:6).

The main constraint for GruntWorx is that the existing connection/client substrate assumes OAuth access and refresh tokens and a shared grant lifecycle. Its authentication model must be checked against that contract; adding its namespace to `ADAPTERS` alone would not complete the integration.
